results.title: Elementary topos
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A category $E$ is an elementary topos if it has all finite limits, it admits a cartesian monoidal structure for which it is monoidal closed (that is, $E$ is cartesian closed), and it has a subobject classifier.

results.title: Fundamental theorem of topos theory
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $E$ is an elementary topos and $X$ is an object of $E$, then the slice category $E/X$ of objects of $E$ over $X$ is again an elementary topos.

results.title: Groups satisfying a set of laws
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $W$ be a set of words in the free group on countably many generators $x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots$. A group $G$ satisfies the laws in $W$ when every homomorphism from this free group to $G$ sends every $w \in W$ to $1$. The groups satisfying $W$ form the variety defined by $W$, and every variety arises this way.

results.title: Composite terms of the Lucas sequence $U_n(3, -4)$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $U_n = U_n(3, -4)$ be the Lucas sequence with $U_0 = 0$, $U_1 = 1$ and $U_{n+2} = 3U_{n+1} + 4U_n$, so that $U_n = 0, 1, 3, 13, 51, 205, 819, \ldots$. For every natural number $n \ge 4$, $U_n$ is composite: $U_n > 1$ and $U_n$ is not prime.

results.title: Unit shifts of $U_n(P, 1)$ are eventually composite
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $P \ge 3$ be an integer and let $U_n = U_n(P, 1)$ be the Lucas sequence with $U_0 = 0$, $U_1 = 1$ and $U_{n+2} = PU_{n+1} - U_n$. Then there is a natural number $N$ such that for every $n \ge N$ the three integers $U_n - 1$, $U_n$ and $U_n + 1$ are all composite, that is, each is greater than $1$ and not prime.

results.title: A shift of $U_n(P, -1)$ away from primes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $P \ge 1$ be an integer and let $U_n = U_n(P, -1)$ be the Lucas sequence with $U_0 = 0$, $U_1 = 1$ and $U_{n+2} = PU_{n+1} + U_n$. Then there is an integer $K > 0$ such that for every natural number $n$ the three integers $U_n + K - 1$, $U_n + K$ and $U_n + K + 1$ are all composite, that is, each is greater than $1$ and not prime.

results.title: Lucas sequences with square $Q$ have finitely many prime terms
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $P$ and $Q$ be integers with $P \ge 1$ and $P^2 - 4Q > 0$, where $Q \ne 0$ is a perfect square, and let $U_n = U_n(P, Q)$ be the Lucas sequence with $U_0 = 0$, $U_1 = 1$ and $U_{n+2} = PU_{n+1} - QU_n$. Then $|U_n|$ is prime for only finitely many natural numbers $n$.

results.title: Lucas sequences with power parameters have finitely many prime terms
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $x \ne y$ be real numbers such that $x + y$ and $xy$ are integers, and let $r > 1$ be a natural number. Let $P$ and $Q$ be integers with $P = x^r + y^r$ and $Q = x^r y^r$, and suppose $Q \ne 0$, $P \ge 1$ and $P^2 - 4Q > 0$. Let $U_n = U_n(P, Q)$ be the Lucas sequence with $U_0 = 0$, $U_1 = 1$ and $U_{n+2} = PU_{n+1} - QU_n$. Then $|U_n|$ is prime for only finitely many natural numbers $n$.

results.title: Antimultiplicative arithmetical functions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $R$ be a type with a zero and a one. An arithmetical function $f$ with values in $R$ is antimultiplicative if $f(1) = 1$ and $f(p^k) = 0$ for every prime $p$ and every integer $k \ge 1$.

results.title: The Dirichlet identity is antimultiplicative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every semiring $R$, the identity $\delta$ of Dirichlet convolution on arithmetical functions with values in $R$, given by $\delta(1) = 1$ and $\delta(n) = 0$ for $n \ne 1$, is antimultiplicative.

results.title: Antimultiplicative functions vanish at primes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a type with a zero and a one, and let $f$ be an antimultiplicative arithmetical function with values in $R$. Then $f(p) = 0$ for every prime $p$.

results.title: Multiplicative and antimultiplicative units form subgroups
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $U$ be the group of units of the ring of real arithmetical functions under Dirichlet convolution. The units $f$ with $f(1) = 1$, the multiplicative units and the antimultiplicative units form subgroups $U_1$, $U_M$ and $U_A$ of $U$, respectively. Moreover $U_M \le U_1$, $U_A \le U_1$ and $U_M \cap U_A = \{\delta\}$, where $\delta$ is the Dirichlet identity.

results.title: Unique splitting into multiplicative and antimultiplicative parts
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every real arithmetical function $f$ with $f(1) = 1$ can be written in exactly one way as a Dirichlet convolution $f = g * h$ of a multiplicative real arithmetical function $g$ and an antimultiplicative real arithmetical function $h$.

results.title: Every integer is a sum of five cubes of polynomials
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every integer $N$ there are polynomials $f, g, h, k, l \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$, each of degree at least $1$, such that $f^3 + g^3 + h^3 + k^3 + l^3 = N$ as an identity in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$.

results.title: Conjugates
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The conjugates of a complex number $\alpha$ are the roots in $\mathbb{C}$ of its minimal polynomial over $\mathbb{Q}$, counted with multiplicity. If $\alpha$ is transcendental, its minimal polynomial is taken to be $0$ and it has no conjugates.

results.title: Degree of a complex number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The degree of a complex number $\alpha$ is the degree of its minimal polynomial over $\mathbb{Q}$. If $\alpha$ is transcendental, its minimal polynomial is taken to be $0$, so its degree is $0$.

results.title: Trace as the sum of conjugates
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $\alpha \in \mathbb{C}$, the trace of $\alpha$ is the sum of its conjugates, that is, of the roots in $\mathbb{C}$ of the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, counted with multiplicity. For transcendental $\alpha$ there are no conjugates and the trace is $0$.

results.title: Absolute trace
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The absolute trace of a complex number $\alpha$ is the real number obtained by dividing the real part of the trace of $\alpha$ by the degree of $\alpha$. If $\alpha$ is transcendental, its trace and its degree are both $0$, and its absolute trace is taken to be $0$.

results.title: Totally positive algebraic integers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A complex number $\alpha$ is a totally positive algebraic integer when it is integral over $\mathbb{Z}$ and every conjugate of $\alpha$ (every root in $\mathbb{C}$ of its minimal polynomial over $\mathbb{Q}$) is a strictly positive real number.

results.title: The trace of a totally positive algebraic integer has positive real part
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $\alpha \in \mathbb{C}$ is a totally positive algebraic integer, then the real part of the trace of $\alpha$ is strictly positive.

results.title: The trace of a totally positive algebraic integer is real
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $\alpha \in \mathbb{C}$ is a totally positive algebraic integer, then the imaginary part of the trace of $\alpha$ is $0$.

results.title: Positivity of the absolute trace
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a complex number $\alpha$ is a totally positive algebraic integer, then the absolute trace of $\alpha$ is strictly positive.

results.title: Minimal polynomial of one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The minimal polynomial of $1 \in \mathbb{C}$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ is $X - 1$.

results.title: One is a totally positive algebraic integer
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The complex number $1$ is a totally positive algebraic integer.

results.title: Admissible trace bounds
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A real number $\rho$ is admissible when $\rho \ge 0$ and only finitely many totally positive algebraic integers $\alpha \in \mathbb{C}$ have absolute trace less than $\rho$.

results.title: Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace constant
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace constant $C_{86}$ is the supremum, taken in the extended reals, of the admissible real bounds: the real numbers $\rho \ge 0$ such that only finitely many complex numbers that are totally positive algebraic integers have absolute trace less than $\rho$.

results.title: Admissible bounds lie below the Schur–Siegel–Smyth constant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $C_{86}$ be the Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace constant, an extended real number. Every admissible real number $\rho$ satisfies $\rho \le C_{86}$ in the extended reals.

results.title: Upper bounds for the Schur–Siegel–Smyth constant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every extended real number $b$, the Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace constant is at most $b$ if and only if every admissible real number $c$ satisfies $c \le b$.

path: Max-min indecomposable sequences and lunar primes

results.title: Max-min product
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The max-min product of sequences $g, h \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is the sequence $g \otimes h$ with $(g \otimes h)_k = \max_{i + j = k} \min(g_i, h_j)$ for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the maximum running over pairs of natural numbers $(i, j)$. This is the product of the max-min semiring $(\mathbb{N}, \max, \min)$ on coefficient sequences.

results.title: Constant coefficient of a max-min product
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all sequences $g, h \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, the max-min product satisfies $(g \otimes h)_0 = \min(g_0, h_0)$.

results.title: Linear coefficient of a max-min product
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all sequences $g, h \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, the max-min product satisfies $(g \otimes h)_1 = \max(\min(g_0, h_1), \min(g_1, h_0))$.

results.title: Monomials over the max-min semiring
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A coefficient sequence $g : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ over the max-min semiring is a monomial when exactly one of its entries is nonzero, that is, when it is $c x^i$ for some index $i$ and some coefficient $c \neq 0$.

results.title: The zero sequence is not a monomial
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The zero coefficient sequence $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is not a max-min monomial: a monomial has exactly one nonzero entry, and the zero sequence has none.

results.title: Max-min indecomposable sequences
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A coefficient sequence $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is indecomposable (in the arXiv version: irreducible) when for all sequences $g, h : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $g \otimes h = f$, where $\otimes$ is the max-min product, $g$ or $h$ is a max-min monomial, that is, a sequence with exactly one nonzero term.

results.title: The zero sequence is decomposable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The zero coefficient sequence $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is not indecomposable over the max-min semiring: it factors as $0 = 0 \otimes 0$, where $\otimes$ is the max-min product, and the zero sequence is not a monomial.

results.title: Coefficient sequence of a digit string
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n$ and $b$ be natural numbers. The coefficient sequence of a digit string $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ with digits in $\{0, \dots, b - 1\}$ is the sequence $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ whose $k$-th term is $a_k$ for $k < n$ and $0$ for $k \ge n$.

results.title: A digit string has no coefficients beyond its length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ and $b$ be natural numbers and let $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ be a digit string with digits in $\{0, \dots, b - 1\}$. Then for every $k \ge n$, the $k$-th term of the coefficient sequence of $a$ is $0$.

results.title: Lunar unit
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $b$, the lunar unit of base $b$ is the coefficient sequence $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ whose constant term is $b - 1$ and whose other terms are all $0$, that is, the constant polynomial $b - 1$ over the max-min semiring. The subtraction is truncated, so the lunar unit of base $0$ is the zero sequence.

results.title: The lunar unit is a monomial
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $b \ge 2$, the lunar unit of base $b$, the sequence with constant term $b - 1$ and all other terms $0$, is a max-min monomial: it has exactly one nonzero term.

results.title: Lunar primes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $b$ be a natural number. The lunar unit of base $b$ is the constant polynomial $b - 1$, the sequence with constant term $b - 1$ and all other terms $0$. A coefficient sequence $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is a lunar prime of base $b$ (Applegate, LeBrun and Sloane) when for all sequences $g, h : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with all terms less than $b$ and $g \otimes h = f$, where $\otimes$ is the max-min…

results.title: Zero is not a lunar prime
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every integer $b \ge 2$, the zero sequence is not a lunar prime of base $b$: $0 = 0 \otimes 0$, where $\otimes$ is the max-min product, and $0$ is not the lunar unit, the constant polynomial $b - 1$ with coefficient sequence $(b - 1, 0, 0, \dots)$.

results.title: Lunar prime candidates
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $b$ be a natural number. A coefficient sequence $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is a prime candidate in base $b$ when its constant term $f_0$ is nonzero and some term $f_i$ equals $b - 1$, where the subtraction is truncated, so that $b - 1 = 0$ when $b = 0$. For $f$ with all terms less than $b$, the second condition says that the largest coefficient of $f$ is $b - 1$.

results.title: The lunar unit is a prime candidate
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $b \ge 2$, the lunar unit of base $b$, the sequence with constant term $b - 1$ and all other terms $0$, is a prime candidate in base $b$: its constant term is nonzero and one of its terms equals $b - 1$.

results.title: Shitov's theorem: almost all Boolean polynomials with nonzero constant term are prime
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, consider the Boolean polynomials of degree exactly $n$ with nonzero constant term, that is, the base-$2$ lunar numbers given by digit strings $(a_0, \dots, a_n) \in \{0, 1\}^{n+1}$ with $a_0 \ne 0$ and $a_n \ne 0$. The proportion of these which are lunar primes in base $2$ tends to $1$ as $n \to \infty$.

results.title: Almost all max-min polynomials are indecomposable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Fix an integer $b \ge 2$. For each $n$, among the polynomials of degree $n$ with coefficients in $\mathcal{B}_b = \{0, \dots, b - 1\}$, that is, coefficient strings $(a_0, \dots, a_n)$ with $a_n \ne 0$, the proportion of those that are indecomposable over the max-min semiring tends to $1$ as $n \to \infty$.

results.title: Asymptotic count of lunar primes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Fix an integer $b \ge 2$. For $n \ge 1$ let $\pi_b(n)$ be the number of digit strings $(a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ with $a_k \in \{0, \dots, b - 1\}$ and leading digit $a_{n-1} \ne 0$ whose coefficient sequence $(a_0, \dots, a_{n-1}, 0, 0, \dots)$ is a lunar prime of base $b$; these are the prime lunar numbers of base $b$ with $n$ digits. Then $\pi_b(n) \sim (b - 1)^2 b^{n-2}$ as $n \to \infty$, as conjectured by…

results.title: Monotone digit maps are lunar homomorphisms
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $d : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be nondecreasing, and for a coefficient sequence $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ write $d(f)$ for the sequence $k \mapsto d(f_k)$. Write $f \oplus g$ for the pointwise maximum and $f \otimes g$ for the max-min product of coefficient sequences $f$ and $g$. Then for all $f$ and $g$, $d(f) \oplus d(g) = d(f \oplus g)$ and $d(f) \otimes d(g) = d(f \otimes g)$.

results.title: Counting Boolean factor pairs with a small sumset
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers with $0 < k \le n$, and let $d > 0$ be a real number. Then the number of pairs $(A, B)$ of finite sets of natural numbers such that $0 \in A$, the largest element of $A$ is $k$, the largest element of $B$ is $n - k$, and $|A + B| \le |A| + |B| + d$, where $A + B = \{a + b : a \in A, b \in B\}$ is the sumset, is at most $n^{2d+2} 2^k$.

results.title: Indecomposable prime candidates are lunar primes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ and $b \ge 2$ be natural numbers, let $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ be a digit string with digits in $\{0, \dots, b - 1\}$, and let $f$ be its coefficient sequence. If $f$ is a prime candidate in base $b$ and $f$ is max-min indecomposable, then $f$ is a lunar prime of base $b$.

results.title: Level counts of a lunar number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $f$ be a lunar number of base $b$ and degree at most $n$, with digits $c_0, \dots, c_n \in \{0, \dots, b - 1\}$, and let $i$ be a natural number. The level count $|f_i|$ is the number of indices $k \le n$ with $c_k \ge i$, that is, the number of nonzero coefficients of the $i$-level support $f_i = s_i(f)$, the Boolean polynomial with coefficient $1$ at $x^k$ when $c_k \ge i$ and $0$ otherwise.

results.title: Level counts of $1 \oplus 2x^2$ in base $3$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For the base-$3$ lunar number $f = 1 \oplus 2x^2$ of degree at most $2$, with digits $1, 0, 2$, exactly two digits are at least $1$ and exactly one digit is at least $2$: $|f_1| = 2$ and $|f_2| = 1$.

results.title: Decomposable lunar numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $b$ and $n$, let $\mathcal{L}_b^n$ be the set of lunar numbers of base $b$ and degree at most $n$, that is, polynomials $c_0 \oplus c_1 x \oplus \dots \oplus c_n x^n$ with digits $c_k \in \{0, \dots, b - 1\}$. The set $\Sigma_b^n$ of decomposable lunar numbers consists of the $h \in \mathcal{L}_b^n$ that factor as $h = f \otimes g$ under the max-min product, with $f, g \in \mathcal{L}_b^n$ each…

results.title: Level-decomposable lunar numbers

results.title: Recurrence for the guesses of permutation Wordle

results.title: Permutation Wordle games solved in a given number of guesses

results.title: Games won with the first guess

results.title: Cyclic shift strategy
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A strategy assigns to each $m$ a permutation of $m$ positions, used to rearrange the entries on the $m$ incorrect positions of a guess. results.title: Components of the cyclic shift strategy
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $m$, the component of the cyclic shift strategy on $m$ positions is the rotation $i \mapsto i + 1 \pmod m$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, m-1\}$.

results.title: Cyclic shift left strategy

results.title: Top component of the left-shift strategy

results.title: Non-top components of the left-shift strategy

results.title: Generalized Rascal numbers as sums of products of binomial coefficients
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $j$, $n$ and $k$ with $k \le n$, the generalized Rascal number $R^{(j)}_{n,k}$, the number of binary words of length $n$ with exactly $k$ ones and at most $j$ ascents (positions where a $0$ is immediately followed by a $1$), equals $\sum_{i=0}^{j} \binom{k}{i} \binom{n-k}{i}$.

results.title: Instances of MAXIMUM k-CUT
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: An instance of MAXIMUM k-CUT is a quadruple $(n, E, k, K)$ of a natural number $n$ (the number of vertices), a finite list $E$ of ordered pairs of natural numbers (the edges), a natural number $k$ (the number of parts) and a natural number $K$ (the bound).

results.title: Well-formed MAXIMUM k-CUT instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance $(n, E, k, K)$ of MAXIMUM k-CUT is well formed when the list $E$ has no repeated entries and every pair $(u, v)$ in $E$ satisfies $u < n$, $v < n$ and $u \ne v$, and the reversed pair $(v, u)$ does not occur in $E$.

results.title: Feasible MAXIMUM k-CUT instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance $(n, E, k, K)$ of MAXIMUM k-CUT is feasible when there are a list $(a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ of $n$ natural numbers, each less than $k$, and a list $C$ of length at least $K$ obtained from $E$ by deleting zero or more of its entries, such that $a_u \ne a_v$ for every pair $(u, v)$ in $C$, where $a_w$ is read as $0$ when $w \ge n$.

results.title: MAXIMUM k-CUT as a decision problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The decision problem MAXIMUM k-CUT accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when decoding $x$ with the canonical bitstring encoding of instances of MAXIMUM k-CUT succeeds and yields an instance that is well formed and feasible. All other bitstrings, including those that fail to decode, are rejected.

results.title: MAXIMUM k-CUT is NP-complete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The decision problem MAXIMUM k-CUT lies in NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to MAXIMUM k-CUT.
